name: Practice Paper 2
subtitle: RRB Radiographer / X-Ray Technician — Full CBT Mock

subsections.title: CT, MRI, USG, Nuclear Medicine & Patient Care

questions.subject: Human Anatomy & Physiology
questions.question: How many pairs of ribs are present in a normal human?
questions.explanation: There are 12 pairs: 7 true (1–7), 3 false (8–10) and 2 floating (11–12).

questions.subject: Human Anatomy & Physiology
questions.question: Which ribs are called 'floating ribs'?
questions.explanation: Ribs 11 and 12 have no anterior attachment to the sternum or costal cartilage.

questions.subject: Human Anatomy & Physiology
questions.question: Which is the smallest bone in the human body?
questions.explanation: The stapes of the middle ear is about 3 mm long.

questions.subject: Human Anatomy & Physiology
questions.question: The hyoid bone lies at approximately the level of which vertebra?
questions.explanation: The hyoid lies at about C3 and does not articulate with any other bone.

questions.subject: Human Anatomy & Physiology
questions.question: The dens (odontoid process) is a part of which vertebra?
questions.explanation: The dens projects upward from the axis and forms a pivot joint with the atlas.

questions.subject: Human Anatomy & Physiology
questions.question: The hip bone (os coxae) is formed by the fusion of:
questions.explanation: The three bones meet and fuse at the acetabulum by about 16–18 years.

questions.subject: Human Anatomy & Physiology
questions.question: Bile is produced by the:
questions.explanation: The liver produces bile; the gall bladder only stores and concentrates it.

questions.subject: Human Anatomy & Physiology
questions.question: Which is the largest gland in the human body?
questions.explanation: The liver weighs about 1.5 kg in adults and is the largest gland.

questions.subject: Human Anatomy & Physiology
questions.question: The mastoid process is a part of which bone?
questions.explanation: The mastoid process of the temporal bone contains the mastoid air cells, which are shown by Law/Schuller and Stenvers views.

questions.subject: Human Anatomy & Physiology
questions.question: How many bones are there in one human hand (carpals, metacarpals and phalanges)?
questions.explanation: 8 carpals + 5 metacarpals + 14 phalanges = 27.

questions.subject: Human Anatomy & Physiology
questions.question: The normal respiratory rate of a resting adult is:
questions.explanation: Rates above 20 (tachypnoea) or below 12 (bradypnoea) should be noted during patient care.

questions.subject: Human Anatomy & Physiology
questions.question: The hila of the kidneys lie approximately at the level of:
questions.explanation: The renal hila lie close to the transpyloric plane (L1); the right kidney is slightly lower than the left.

questions.subject: Radiation Physics & X-ray Equipment
questions.question: The conventional unit of radiation exposure (ionisation in air) is the:
questions.explanation: 1 R = 2.58 × 10⁻⁴ C/kg of air. The rad is for absorbed dose, the rem for dose equivalent and the curie for activity.

questions.subject: Radiation Physics & X-ray Equipment
questions.question: What is the SI unit of equivalent dose and effective dose?
questions.explanation: Equivalent dose (Sv) = absorbed dose (Gy) × radiation weighting factor.

questions.subject: Radiation Physics & X-ray Equipment
questions.question: The SI unit of radioactivity, equal to one disintegration per second, is the:
questions.explanation: 1 Ci = 3.7 × 10¹⁰ Bq.

questions.subject: Radiation Physics & X-ray Equipment
questions.question: The energy of an X-ray photon is:
options: Proportional to the square of wavelength
questions.explanation: E = hc/λ, so shorter wavelength means higher energy and more penetration.

questions.subject: Radiation Physics & X-ray Equipment
questions.question: The half-value layer (HVL) is the thickness of an absorber that:
options: Reduces the beam intensity to half of its original value
Reduces the beam's wavelength by half
questions.explanation: HVL is used to describe beam quality; a harder beam has a larger HVL.

questions.subject: Radiation Physics & X-ray Equipment
questions.question: The main purpose of a rotating anode is to:
options: Reduce the size of the filament
Spread the heat over a larger area so higher exposures can be used
questions.explanation: The focal track spreads heat over a ring-shaped area, which greatly increases tube rating.

questions.subject: Radiation Physics & X-ray Equipment
questions.question: The rotating anode in a diagnostic X-ray tube typically rotates at about:
questions.explanation: Standard anodes run at about 3,000–3,600 rpm and high-speed anodes at about 9,000–10,000 rpm.

questions.subject: Radiation Physics & X-ray Equipment
questions.question: The oil surrounding the X-ray tube inside the housing acts as:
options: An electrical insulator and a medium for heat dissipation
A filter for low-energy X-rays only
questions.explanation: The oil insulates the high-voltage parts and carries heat from the insert to the housing.

questions.subject: Radiation Physics & X-ray Equipment
questions.question: The cloud of electrons that forms around a heated filament is called the:
questions.explanation: The space charge limits further electron emission at low kVp (the space charge effect).

questions.subject: Radiation Physics & X-ray Equipment
questions.question: A single-phase full-wave bridge rectifier in an X-ray generator uses:
questions.explanation: A bridge of four diodes directs both half-cycles of AC through the tube in the same direction.

questions.subject: Radiation Physics & X-ray Equipment
questions.question: Which type of X-ray generator has the lowest voltage ripple?
questions.explanation: Approximate ripple: single-phase 100%, 3-phase 6-pulse ~13%, 12-pulse ~4%, high-frequency <1%.

questions.subject: Radiation Physics & X-ray Equipment
questions.question: The probability of photoelectric absorption is approximately proportional to:
questions.explanation: Photoelectric absorption rises steeply with atomic number and falls sharply with photon energy. This is why bone and contrast media appear white.

questions.subject: Radiation Physics & X-ray Equipment
questions.question: In Compton scattering, the electron ejected from the outer shell is called the:
questions.explanation: The incident photon gives part of its energy to an outer-shell electron, which recoils, and the photon scatters with lower energy.

questions.subject: Radiation Physics & X-ray Equipment
questions.question: Grid cut-off across the entire image is most commonly caused by:
questions.explanation: An inverted focused grid absorbs most of the primary beam at the periphery, giving a light image with only a central strip exposed.

questions.subject: Radiation Physics & X-ray Equipment
questions.question: The moving grid mechanism used to blur out grid lines is called the:
questions.explanation: Moving the grid during exposure removes the visible grid-line pattern.

questions.subject: Radiation Physics & X-ray Equipment
questions.question: The modern hot-cathode (vacuum) X-ray tube was introduced in 1913 by:
questions.explanation: The Coolidge tube used a heated tungsten filament in a high vacuum, which allowed independent control of kVp and mA.

questions.subject: Clinical Radiography — Positioning
questions.question: For a PA chest radiograph, the central ray is centred at the level of:
options: T7 (about the inferior angle of the scapula)
questions.explanation: Centring at T7 places the central ray at the middle of the lung fields.

questions.subject: Clinical Radiography — Positioning
questions.question: In a PA chest radiograph, the scapulae are moved off the lung fields by:
options: Raising both arms above the head
Placing the arms by the side, palms forward
Placing the backs of the hands on the hips and rolling the shoulders forward
Folding the arms across the chest
questions.explanation: Internal rotation of the arms with shoulders forward rotates the scapulae laterally, clear of the lungs.

questions.subject: Clinical Radiography — Positioning
questions.question: For a routine lateral chest radiograph, which side is placed against the image receptor?
options: The side with no pathology only
questions.explanation: With the left side against the IR, the heart lies closer to the film and is magnified less.

questions.subject: Clinical Radiography — Positioning
questions.question: The Stenvers projection is used to demonstrate the:
options: Petrous ridge and internal auditory canal
questions.explanation: Stenvers (posterior profile) shows the petrous portion in profile, including the IAM and mastoid tip.

questions.subject: Clinical Radiography — Positioning
questions.question: The Rhese projection (parieto-orbital oblique) is used to demonstrate the:
questions.explanation: The optic canal is projected end-on into the lower outer quadrant of the orbit.

questions.subject: Clinical Radiography — Positioning
questions.question: The open-mouth Waters projection additionally demonstrates the:
questions.explanation: With the mouth open, the sphenoid sinus is projected through the open mouth.

questions.subject: Clinical Radiography — Positioning
questions.question: For the AP axial projection of the clavicle, the central ray is angled:
questions.explanation: Cephalic angulation projects the clavicle above the scapula and upper ribs.

questions.subject: Clinical Radiography — Positioning
questions.question: The scapular 'Y' view is mainly used to assess:
questions.explanation: In the scapular Y view the humeral head should sit over the centre of the Y; displacement shows anterior or posterior dislocation.

questions.subject: Clinical Radiography — Positioning
questions.question: The tangential carpal canal (Gaynor–Hart) projection demonstrates the:
options: Carpal tunnel, including the hook of hamate and pisiform
questions.explanation: The wrist is hyperextended and the beam is angled along the palm to show the carpal canal end-on.

questions.subject: Clinical Radiography — Positioning
questions.question: For a PA oblique projection of the hand, the hand is rotated:
questions.explanation: A 45° oblique separates the metacarpals and phalanges without overlap.

questions.subject: Clinical Radiography — Positioning
questions.question: For the axial (plantodorsal) projection of the calcaneum, the central ray is angled:
options: 40° cephalad to the long axis of the foot
questions.explanation: A 40° cephalic angle shows the calcaneus from the plantar surface to the subtalar joint.

questions.subject: Clinical Radiography — Positioning
questions.question: To obtain an ankle mortise view, the leg and foot are internally rotated by:
questions.explanation: Internal rotation of 15°–20° brings the intermalleolar line parallel to the IR and opens the entire mortise.

questions.subject: Clinical Radiography — Positioning
questions.question: The tangential ('skyline'/'sunrise') projection of the knee demonstrates the:
questions.explanation: It shows the patella and the femoral trochlear groove tangentially.

questions.subject: Clinical Radiography — Positioning
questions.question: For an AP pelvis, both feet are internally rotated 15°–20° in order to:
options: Place the femoral necks in profile
questions.explanation: Internal rotation corrects the natural anteversion of the femoral neck so its full length is seen.

questions.subject: Clinical Radiography — Positioning
questions.question: A plain KUB radiograph must include the lower border of the:
questions.explanation: The image must include the kidneys above and the bladder down to the symphysis pubis below.

questions.subject: Clinical Radiography — Positioning
questions.question: A lateral cervical spine radiograph is usually taken at an FFD of:
questions.explanation: The shoulder causes a large OFD, so a longer FFD reduces magnification and unsharpness.

questions.subject: Image Processing, Darkroom & Image Quality
questions.question: The X-ray developer solution is:
questions.explanation: The developing agents work only in an alkaline medium; the fixer is acidic.

questions.subject: Image Processing, Darkroom & Image Quality
questions.question: The accelerator (activator) in an X-ray developer is:
questions.explanation: Sodium carbonate (or hydroxide) provides alkalinity and swells the gelatin so the reducing agents can work.

questions.subject: Image Processing, Darkroom & Image Quality
questions.question: The hardening agent in a manual X-ray fixer is:
questions.explanation: Potassium (or chrome) alum hardens the gelatin to prevent scratches and help drying.

questions.subject: Image Processing, Darkroom & Image Quality
questions.question: The acidifier in an X-ray fixer solution is:
questions.explanation: Acetic acid neutralises carried-over developer (stopping development) and keeps the fixer acidic.

questions.subject: Image Processing, Darkroom & Image Quality
questions.question: The theory that explains formation of the latent image in film emulsion is the:
questions.explanation: Gurney–Mott: photoelectrons collect at sensitivity specks and attract silver ions, forming latent image centres.

questions.subject: Image Processing, Darkroom & Image Quality
questions.question: The light-sensitive crystals in a radiographic film emulsion are mainly:
options: Silver bromide (with a little silver iodide)
questions.explanation: The emulsion is about 95% silver bromide and 5% silver iodide crystals suspended in gelatin.

questions.subject: Image Processing, Darkroom & Image Quality
questions.question: Static electricity artefacts on X-ray film usually appear as:
options: Black tree-like, crown or smudge marks
questions.explanation: Static discharge exposes the film. It is common when humidity is low and films are pulled quickly.

questions.subject: Image Processing, Darkroom & Image Quality
questions.question: Spatial resolution of an imaging system is expressed in:
questions.explanation: Higher lp/mm means finer detail can be resolved.

questions.subject: Radiation Protection, Contrast & Special Procedures
questions.question: ALARA stands for:
questions.explanation: ALARA is the principle of optimisation: keep doses as low as reasonably achievable.

questions.subject: Radiation Protection, Contrast & Special Procedures
questions.question: The three cardinal principles of external radiation protection are:
questions.explanation: Minimise time, maximise distance and use shielding. (Justification–optimisation–limitation are the system-of-protection principles.)

questions.subject: Radiation Protection, Contrast & Special Procedures
questions.question: Once pregnancy is declared, the dose to the embryo/fetus of a radiation worker should not exceed about:
options: 20 mSv for the remainder of the pregnancy
1 mSv for the remainder of the pregnancy
questions.explanation: The fetus is protected to about the same level as a member of the public.

questions.subject: Radiation Protection, Contrast & Special Procedures
questions.question: The international radiation warning symbol (trefoil) is shown as:
options: A red cross on a white background
A magenta or black trefoil on a yellow background
A green circle on a black background
A blue triangle on a white background
questions.explanation: The yellow background with a magenta or black trefoil is the standard radiation sign.

questions.subject: Radiation Protection, Contrast & Special Procedures
questions.question: A double-contrast barium enema uses:
questions.explanation: Barium coats the mucosa and gas distends the bowel, showing fine mucosal detail.

questions.subject: Radiation Protection, Contrast & Special Procedures
questions.question: Water-soluble iodinated contrast used for IVU is excreted mainly by:
questions.explanation: Contrast is filtered at the glomerulus and concentrated in the tubules, making the collecting system opaque.

questions.subject: Radiation Protection, Contrast & Special Procedures
questions.question: Before giving IV iodinated contrast for IVU or CT, the most important blood test to check is:
questions.explanation: Impaired renal function (low eGFR) increases the risk of contrast-induced kidney injury.

questions.subject: Radiation Protection, Contrast & Special Procedures
questions.question: A micturating cystourethrogram (MCU) is mainly done to detect:
questions.explanation: Contrast is filled into the bladder and imaged during voiding to show reflux and the urethra.

questions.subject: Radiation Protection, Contrast & Special Procedures
questions.question: In a patient on metformin who receives iodinated contrast, the main concern is:
options: Lactic acidosis if renal function deteriorates
questions.explanation: Metformin is excreted by the kidneys, so contrast-induced renal impairment can cause metformin build-up and lactic acidosis.

questions.subject: Radiation Protection, Contrast & Special Procedures
questions.question: ERCP is used to demonstrate the:
questions.explanation: Endoscopic Retrograde Cholangio-Pancreatography: contrast is injected through the ampulla of Vater.

questions.subject: CT, MRI, USG, Nuclear Medicine & Patient Care
questions.question: What is the CT number of air?
questions.explanation: Air is −1000, fat about −100, water 0, soft tissue +20 to +60 and dense bone up to about +1000 HU.

questions.subject: CT, MRI, USG, Nuclear Medicine & Patient Care
questions.question: Continuous rotation of the gantry in helical (spiral) CT was made possible by:
questions.explanation: Slip rings carry power and data without cables, so the tube can rotate continuously.

questions.subject: CT, MRI, USG, Nuclear Medicine & Patient Care
questions.question: Third-generation CT scanners use which tube–detector motion?
questions.explanation: Both the tube and a curved detector array rotate together around the patient.

questions.subject: CT, MRI, USG, Nuclear Medicine & Patient Care
questions.question: The strength of the main magnetic field of an MRI scanner is measured in:
questions.explanation: Clinical MRI commonly uses 1.5 T or 3 T. 1 T = 10,000 gauss.

questions.subject: CT, MRI, USG, Nuclear Medicine & Patient Care
questions.question: Gadolinium-based contrast agents are used in:
questions.explanation: Gadolinium is paramagnetic. It shortens T1 relaxation, so enhancing tissue appears bright on T1-weighted images.

questions.subject: CT, MRI, USG, Nuclear Medicine & Patient Care
questions.question: Doppler ultrasound is used mainly to measure:
questions.explanation: A moving reflector (blood) changes the frequency of the returning echo, and this shift gives the velocity.

questions.subject: CT, MRI, USG, Nuclear Medicine & Patient Care
questions.question: Ultrasound gel is applied between the transducer and the skin in order to:
options: Remove air and provide acoustic coupling
questions.explanation: Air reflects almost all ultrasound, so the gel lets sound pass into the body.

questions.subject: CT, MRI, USG, Nuclear Medicine & Patient Care
questions.question: Under the Bio-Medical Waste Management Rules, 2016, human anatomical waste is collected in a:
questions.explanation: Yellow: anatomical and soiled waste (incineration). Red: contaminated plastics. White: sharps. Blue: glassware.

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.question: India's first electric train ran on 3 February 1925 between:
questions.explanation: The first electric train ran on the Harbour line from Victoria Terminus to Kurla.

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.question: The first Vande Bharat Express (2019) was flagged off between:
questions.explanation: The first Vande Bharat (Train 18) started service between New Delhi and Varanasi in February 2019.

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.question: On which date did the Constituent Assembly adopt the Constitution of India?
questions.explanation: It was adopted on 26 November 1949 (Constitution Day) and came into force on 26 January 1950.

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.question: Who is known as the chief architect (father) of the Indian Constitution?
questions.explanation: Dr Ambedkar was Chairman of the Drafting Committee. Dr Rajendra Prasad presided over the Constituent Assembly.

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.question: Which is the largest state of India by area?
questions.explanation: Rajasthan covers about 3.42 lakh sq km, roughly 10.4% of India's area.

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.question: The Jallianwala Bagh massacre took place in:
questions.explanation: It happened on 13 April 1919 at Amritsar, under General Dyer.

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.question: Kaziranga National Park, famous for the one-horned rhinoceros, is located in:
questions.explanation: Kaziranga is a UNESCO World Heritage Site in Assam.

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.question: What is the currency of Japan?
questions.explanation: Yuan is China's, Won is Korea's and Ringgit is Malaysia's currency.

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.question: The Ranji Trophy is associated with:
questions.explanation: The Ranji Trophy is India's premier domestic first-class cricket championship.

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.question: Who was the first Indian to win a Nobel Prize?
questions.explanation: Tagore won the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1913 for Gitanjali.

questions.subject: General Arithmetic, Intelligence & Reasoning
questions.question: Two numbers are in the ratio 3 : 5 and their sum is 64. What is the larger number?
questions.explanation: 8 parts = 64, so 1 part = 8, and the larger number = 5 × 8 = 40.

questions.subject: General Arithmetic, Intelligence & Reasoning
questions.question: What is the compound interest on ₹10,000 at 10% per annum for 2 years, compounded annually?

questions.subject: General Arithmetic, Intelligence & Reasoning
questions.question: If 15% of a number is 45, what is the number?

questions.subject: General Arithmetic, Intelligence & Reasoning
questions.question: An ambulance travels at 60 km/h for 2 hours 30 minutes. What distance does it cover?
questions.explanation: Distance = 60 × 2.5 = 150 km.

questions.subject: General Arithmetic, Intelligence & Reasoning
questions.question: The average of 5 numbers is 20. If one number is removed, the average of the rest becomes 18. What is the removed number?
questions.explanation: Total = 100 and the new total = 4 × 18 = 72, so the removed number = 28.

questions.subject: General Arithmetic, Intelligence & Reasoning
questions.question: A shopkeeper marks goods 20% above cost price and gives a 10% discount. What is his profit percentage?
questions.explanation: 1.20 × 0.90 = 1.08, which is an 8% profit.

questions.subject: General Arithmetic, Intelligence & Reasoning
questions.question: Find the odd one out: 2, 3, 5, 9, 11
questions.explanation: All are prime numbers except 9 (= 3 × 3).

questions.subject: General Arithmetic, Intelligence & Reasoning
questions.question: Eye : Ophthalmologist :: Skin : ?
questions.explanation: An ophthalmologist treats eye disorders and a dermatologist treats skin disorders.

questions.subject: General Arithmetic, Intelligence & Reasoning
questions.question: If ACE = 9 (using letter positions A = 1, C = 3, E = 5), then BDF = ?

questions.subject: General Arithmetic, Intelligence & Reasoning
questions.question: What is the angle between the hour hand and the minute hand of a clock at 3:00?
questions.explanation: Each hour mark is 30°, and 3 × 30° = 90°.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is the SI unit of electric current?
questions.explanation: The ampere is one of the seven SI base units.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which acid is present in the human stomach?
questions.explanation: Gastric HCl kills microbes and activates pepsinogen to pepsin.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which blood group is known as the universal donor?
questions.explanation: O-negative red cells have no A, B or Rh(D) antigens.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which metal is present at the centre of the chlorophyll molecule?
questions.explanation: Chlorophyll has Mg²⁺ at its centre; haemoglobin has iron.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Sound cannot travel through:
questions.explanation: Sound is a mechanical wave and needs a medium to travel.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Most kidney stones are made of:
questions.explanation: Calcium oxalate stones are the most common type, and most are radio-opaque on a KUB.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Rusting of iron requires the presence of:
questions.explanation: Rust is hydrated iron(III) oxide and needs both air (O₂) and water.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is the focal length of a lens of power +2 dioptres?
questions.explanation: f = 1/P = 1/2 m = 50 cm. A positive power means a convex lens.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which vitamin is produced in the skin on exposure to sunlight?
questions.explanation: UV-B converts 7-dehydrocholesterol in the skin into vitamin D3.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which is the hardest naturally occurring substance?
questions.explanation: Diamond is a crystalline form of carbon and scores 10 on the Mohs scale.
